title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. From this page and its neighbours: M_* is a cosimplicial k-module, with M_{[n]} its value on [n]. For a simplicial set X, F_X(M_*) = M_X is the module of 'X-cochains with coefficients in M_*'. Concretely, F_X(M_*) = Hom_Δ(k[X], M_*), the end over Δ, so that F_{Δ^n}(M_*) = M_{[n]}. Limits of simplicial sets go to limits of functors.

(1) The circle. The top line K → F ⇉ F' is a kernel (equalizer) of functors, computed pointwise: K(M_*) → F(M_*) ⇉ F'(M_*). The example is S = Δ^1/∂Δ^1, the simplicial circle (note the arrow Δ^1_* → S). Then F_S = K is the equalizer of F_{Δ^1} ⇉ F_{Δ^0}. Pointwise, K(M_*) = Ker(α*, β*) is the equalizer of the two endpoint restrictions α*, β*: M_{[1]} ⇉ M_{[0]}. So K(M_*) = F_S(K).

(2) Test object. Grothendieck takes Ψ_* = C^0_*, the cosimplicial algebra Ψ_{[n]} = k^{Δ_n} = k^{n+1} of functions on vertices. The previous page uses chains C_n = Λ^{i+1} k^{n+1}, with boundary given by contraction with T_n = Σ e_i. Then:
- K(Ψ_*) = Eq(k^2 ⇉ k) = k (the diagonal).
- The line k ⇒ Λ^2 k^2 ≃ k → 0 with ΛT_2 records the 1-simplex / degree-one part.
- Elements of the form αT_{[n]} + T_n ∧ β, with α ∈ k and β ∈ Ψ_{[n]}, describe Ψ_{[n]} ⊕ Λ^2 Ψ_{[n]}.
- Right column: K(M_*) ≃ Z^0(M ⊗ K^·) ≃ Hom^·(M^∨, K^·) ≃ Hom_*(K_*, M_*). This says K is representable, by the cosimplicial object K_* = k[S] (written K_* ≃ Ψ_* ⊕ Λ^2Ψ_*).

(3) Classifying transformations. Natural transformations u: K = F_S → F_{Δ^n}, i.e. u_M: K(M_*) → M_{[n]}, are classified by Yoneda: one evaluates on the universal case, giving K(P_*) ≃ k → F_{Δ^n}(Ψ_*) ≃ Ψ_{[n]}. Hence Hom(F_S, F_{Δ^n}) ≅ k[S_n], i.e. linear combinations of n-simplices.

(4) Multiplicativity. The big diagram checks compatibility with tensor products. The external product K(M)⊗K(N) → K(M⊗N) is induced by M_{[1]}⊗N_{[1]} → [M⊗N]_1, with degreewise tensor product. A multiplicative transformation satisfies u_{M⊗N}(x·y) = u_M(x)⊗u_N(y), compatible with the projection (M⊗N)_{[n]}.

(5) Coalgebra dictionary. The bottom lines say the same thing in general. For F_M = Hom(M, −), a lax monoidal structure Hom(M,K)⊗Hom(M,L) → Hom(M,K⊗L) is the same as a comultiplication M → M⊗M. Multiplicative transformations therefore correspond to set-like (group-like) elements, those with Δx = x⊗x.

Purpose. This feeds the next page's statements: Hom(Δ^m, Δ^n) ≅ Hom_mult(F_{Δ^n}, F_{Δ^m}), and more generally X_{[n]} ≅ Hom_mult(F_X, F_{Δ^n}). That is a reconstruction of a simplicial set from its multiplicative cochain functor. The proof there uses linear independence of characters (Dedekind/Artin) via prime ideals Ker u_i. Within the 1976 divided-power de Rham project, this fixes the formal framework in which simplicial sets act by 'cochain functors' on cosimplicial (commutative) algebras such as the divided-power de Rham algebras of the simplices.
errors: No substantive error detectable. The notation is loose: K is used both for the kernel functor F_S and for a coefficient object (Hom(M,K)), and K^·, K_* and K are conflated.
The identification K(M_*) ≃ Hom_*(K_*, M_*) is written with arguments in varying order (Hom^·(M^∨,K^·) versus Hom_*(K_*,M_*)). This is only a duality bookkeeping issue.

Recovering S_n as exactly the multiplicative transformations needs the base k to be connected (no nontrivial idempotents), as in the linear-independence-of-characters argument. This hypothesis is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Cochains of a simplicial set X with coefficients in a cosimplicial module, F_X(M_*) = Hom_Δ(k[X], M_*) = M_X, sending colimits of simplicial sets to limits (circle = equalizer of endpoint evaluations).
ideas.modern_name: Coend/end pairing between simplicial sets and cosimplicial objects (Kan extension along Yoneda)

ideas.what: Yoneda classification of natural transformations F_S → F_{Δ^n} by elements of k[S_n], obtained by evaluating on the universal cosimplicial module Ψ_* = C^0_* (vertex functions).
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda lemma / representability of linear functors

ideas.what: A lax monoidal structure on Hom(M, −) is equivalent to a coalgebra structure M → M⊗M. Multiplicative transformations correspond to set-like elements, which yields reconstruction of a simplicial set from its multiplicative cochain functor (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Group-like elements of the coalgebra k[X]; Tannakian-type reconstruction of a set from its linearization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore (Dedekind–Artin independence of characters; coalgebra theory, Sweedler 1969)

ideas.what: Chains of Δ^n modelled as an exterior algebra Λ(k^{n+1}) with differential given by contraction with T = Σe_i; degree-1 part Ψ ⊕ Λ^2Ψ.
ideas.modern_name: Koszul-type model of simplicial chains of the standard simplex

missed.claim: This is a record of Grothendieck's (c. 1975-76) framework for treating simplicial sets through multiplicative 'cochain functors' on cosimplicial algebras, as preparation for his divided-power de Rham complex of simplices. The reconstruction Hom(Δ^m,Δ^n) ≅ Hom_mult(F_{Δ^n},F_{Δ^m}) is elementary. Its interest is historical: it positions the 1976 IHES lecture as an integral, divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms. That line was later pursued by others (e.g. Cenkl–Porter, and Mandell's cochain reconstruction theorems), not credited to Grothendieck.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historically: documents the categorical scaffolding of an unpublished 1976 lecture on integral/divided-power cochain models of homotopy types. The page's mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine Yoneda and coalgebra bookkeeping: the circle as an equalizer, representability of the cochain functor, and multiplicativity corresponding to group-like elements. These serve a reconstruction lemma on the next page. Nothing here would surprise a specialist; the only interest is as context for the unpublished divided-power de Rham lecture.
transcription_corrections: Near Δ^0_* the handwritten word over the arrow u_M to M_{[n]} looks like 'fonctoriel?' rather than illegible.

The arrow Δ^1_* ↓ S indicates S is the circle Δ^1/∂Δ^1; the struck-through symbol before (M_*) on that line is K, so the line reads K(M_*) → M_{[1]} ⇉ M_{[0]} with α*_{M_*}, β*_{M_*}, and K(M_*) = F_S(K).
The right-column first line is K(M_*) ≃ Z^0(M_· ⊗ K^·), with a cocycle Z^0, rather than I^0.
The marginal '[?]T_n ∧ β ∈' appears to read '∂T_n ∧ β ∈ Λ^2Ψ_{[n]}' (uncertain).
The final line M → M⊗M has a crossed-out ⊗ written over, i.e. a diagonal/comultiplication.
